name: Nivolumab (cutaneous melanoma)

biomarkers.note: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy. No positive companion biomarker is required to start; applicable regardless of BRAF status. Used in the adjuvant setting for resected high-risk stage III/IV (CheckMate 238) and in the unresectable/metastatic setting (CheckMate 066/067). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous, Table 14.

lineOfTherapy: adjuvant anti-PD-1 for resected high-risk stage III/IV melanoma, and single-agent anti-PD-1 for unresectable stage III or stage IV melanoma; not BRAF-restricted

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: resected high-risk stage III/IV (adjuvant) OR unresectable stage III / stage IV (advanced)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Nivolumab as adjuvant and advanced-disease anti-PD-1 option; Table 14, MS-55 to MS-56

drugs.name: Nivolumab

provenance.locator: Table 14 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Treatment Regimens, Nivolumab row, MS-55 to MS-56 (lines 8159 to 8161): FDA Prescribing information 240 mg Q2W or 480 mg Q4W; CheckMate 067 (line 8157) 3 mg/kg Q2W

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 14 (MS-55 to MS-56). Nivolumab 240 mg IV flat every 2 weeks (FDA prescribing information), until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Source-stated equivalent: 480 mg Q4W flat (FDA prescribing information); and 3 mg/kg Q2W (CheckMate 066/067). The 480 mg every-4-weeks schedule is modeled here as an accepted alternative in regimen.cycles rather than as a second drug row. In the adjuvant setting nivolumab is given for up to 1 year; in advanced disease continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

regimen.cycles: Adjuvant (resected stage III/IV): nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) for up to 1 year. Advanced (unresectable stage III / stage IV): nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 14, MS-55 to MS-56). The 480 mg Q4W schedule uses a 28-day cycle.
supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) monitoring (thyroid and other endocrinopathies, hepatitis, colitis/diarrhea, pneumonitis, dermatitis, nephritis); manage per NCCN Guidelines for Management of Immunotherapy-Related Toxicities.
Baseline and periodic thyroid (TSH/free T4), liver function, glucose as indicated.

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose) before each cycle and as indicated
symptom review for colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, endocrinopathy
clinical/radiographic response assessment (advanced disease); recurrence surveillance (adjuvant)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold nivolumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; permanent discontinuation for severe/grade 3 to 4 irAE. Obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.locator: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy framework for melanoma; dosing taken from the guideline layer (Table 14, MS-55 to MS-56)

guideline.locator: Table 14 Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Treatment Regimens, Nivolumab (FDA prescribing information 240 mg Q2W or 480 mg Q4W; CheckMate 067 3 mg/kg Q2W), MS-55 to MS-56 (lines 8155 to 8161)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for nivolumab anti-PD-1 monotherapy in cutaneous melanoma, covering both adjuvant therapy for resected high-risk stage III/IV disease and treatment of unresectable stage III or stage IV disease. The dose is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous v2.2026, Table 14 (MS-55 to MS-56): nivolumab 240 mg IV flat every 2 weeks or 480 mg every 4 weeks (FDA prescribing information), with a source-stated weight-based equivalent of 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (CheckMate 066/067). Adjuvant duration is up to 1 year; advanced-disease treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Immune-related adverse event monitoring applies. Every modeled numeric dose is sourced and no field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
